history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 227 (Shree Mahalaxmi Temple, Bandora, Ponda) - same real temple. CSV town 'Ponda' is the taluka; the temple stands at Bandora (Bandivade), ~4 km from Ponda, North Goa. Originated in the 15th century; Portuguese records list the Mahalaxmi (Malcumi) temple at Kolambe near Colva among those destroyed in 1567. During the Inquisition era two devotees (Safto and Fato) smuggled the idol out of Colva in a trunk at night, first to Talauli near Ponda and later to Bandivade, where a small temple was established in 1866 (per lightuptemples). The idol is notable for wearing a linga on its head - a Shakta form recalling the Saraswat Shiva-Shakti worship - and the temple holds one of India's largest galleries of wooden Vishnu images.

name: Shri Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Bandora (Bandivade) is a temple village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 4 km from Ponda town and 28 km from Panaji. It lies in Goa's temple belt along the Zuari river, home to the Ramnath, Nagesh and Mahalaxmi temples, and is known for its calm, green agrarian setting and Konkani temple architecture.

travel.road: Well signposted from Ponda (~4 km); local buses run between Ponda and Bandora; ample parking on site

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant 15-30 degC); Navratri and the annual March-April zatra are the most vibrant times (crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Aartis reported at 7:00 AM, 12:30 PM, 8:00 PM; generally open morning to late evening (verify)
